heroHeadline: Trump Rejects Iran's Ceasefire Offer, Expects to Resume Bombing After Midterms, as Xi Visit Wraps and Press-Ban Fight Continues
heroSubtitle: President Trump rejected a seven-day Iranian ceasefire and Strait of Hormuz proposal and told aides he expects US bombing of Iran to resume after the November midterms, the Wall Street Journal reported Saturday, September 26, 2026 (Day 617), even as he has publicly predicted a deal after the vote. The report came a day after Trump closed out Xi Jinping's three-day state visit — the first by a Chinese leader in nearly three years — with tea in the White House Red Room and a joint tour of the National Archives, following Wednesday's arrival ceremony, state dinner and an extension of the US-China trade truce through January 10, 2027. The visit unfolded against the backdrop of Trump's ongoing ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House grounds: a federal judge restored the outlets' credentials for 14 days on September 24 citing due-process violations, yet CNN and MS NOW editorial staff were still turned away from covering Xi's arrival hours after the ruling, and the White House launched a 24/7 'Trump TV' livestream amid the dispute. Trump's approval remains near career lows, with Reuters/Ipsos and Verasight polls both putting it at 32-33% in the past week.
